Five of the plan's drawing sheets were also viewed directly as images (site/utility plan, SESC plan, storm/sanitary/water-main detail sheets) and are genuine, consistent civil engineering drawings. One small correction was found: the register's P1 item states the steep bluff soil (67F) is 35-70% slopes; the plan's own SSURGO soils table states 26-70%. Everything else checked was accurate.

sites_by_type.note: Site type breakdown requires D-6631-06 Parcel Types sheet; all counts are estimates from lot dimension patterns only

register_items.description: California Drive STA 23+68.74 Low Point, El. 659.22
register_items.consequence: Gravity sewer outlet vs. low-point conflict — lift station need unverified. The storm sewer profile on D-6631-13 establishes the California Drive low point at El. 659.22 (LOW PT ELEV: 659.22, STA 23+68.74). The sanitary sewer on D-6631-23 shows SAN MH #CD5 at STA 24+00 and a "24 LF OF 12" PVC SAN SWR @ -0.50%" stub. The existing sanitary sewer POE connection elevation is not stated anywhere in the readable plan text. If the existing sewer invert at the connection is at or above El. 659.22 (which is plausible for a bluff-edge condition), the gravity system cannot drain and a lift station is required. No lift station is shown, sized, or specified anywhere in the 49-sheet plan set.
register_items.correction: Sanitary sewer system will not drain. Raw sewage will back up to all 155 sites. System will fail on day of first occupancy. A lift station retrofit in a paved collector street is a $150,000–$400,000 change order and a schedule-stopping event.
register_items.resolves: Before any sewer installation: EOR must obtain as-built invert elevation of the existing receiving sewer at the California Drive POE. If existing invert > El. 657.5 (leaving 18" of cover and 0.40% slope headroom), a lift station and force main must be designed, permitted, and added to the bid. Do not allow sanitary sewer installation on California Drive to proceed until this is confirmed in writing.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — mandatory RFI before earthwork.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable if lift station is added: EGLE Act 399 sanitary sewer extension permit must include lift station design, wet well sizing, and force main routing. A lift station changes the permit scope materially.
register_items.rom: RFI to EOR → EOR field investigation → EGLE permit amendment if lift station required → revised bid documents. Inspection hold point: do not open trench on California Drive sanitary until EOR written confirmation of gravity feasibility.

register_items.description: All MH sites (estimated 75–95 sites, type unknown)
register_items.consequence: Electrical service amperage likely undersized for double-wide MH sites. D-6631-49 shows the only readable electrical service detail: "100A/3P MCB, 120/240V, 1Ø-3W" panel. Standard industry and NEC 550.32 practice for manufactured home sites is a 200A, 240V, single-phase, 3-wire service with a 200A meter base/disconnect. A 100A service cannot support a modern double-wide MH (15–20 kW HVAC + 10 kW range + 5 kW water heater + other loads = 30–40A continuous minimum, with starting currents exceeding 100A service capacity during peak demand). D-6631-47 shows "E1" and "E3" parcel designations — if E3 is the 200A MH designation, the single detail shown (D-6631-49) may be E1 only; but no second detail is readable.
register_items.correction: Double-wide MH residents will experience chronic breaker trips, inability to run HVAC and cooking simultaneously, and potential code citation. NEC 550.32(A) requires a minimum 200A service for a manufactured home lot intended for a double-wide. If wired at 100A throughout, must be replaced before occupancy permits are issued. Retrograde rewiring in a finished site costs $3,000–$6,000 per site.
register_items.resolves: Immediate: Submit RFI to EOR requesting the complete electrical service schedule by parcel type. If MH lots (E3 or equivalent) are served by the 100A detail shown, EOR must revise to 200A meter base, 200A main breaker, 2/0-2/0-2/0-1/0 AWG service conductors (or per NEC Table 310.15(B)(16) for 200A), and appropriately sized conduit (minimum 2" PVC). Transformer kVA must be recalculated accordingly.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — mandatory before electrical rough-in.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Service amperage is a code-compliance item reviewed by the electrical inspector and potentially by the utility provider under their interconnection requirements. A revision from 100A to 200A changes transformer sizing and load calculations that may have been submitted for utility approval.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR electrical schedule revision → revised transformer sizing → utility coordination letter. Hold point: no electrical conduit installation until service schedule confirmed.

register_items.description: All streets — turning radii at cul-de-sacs and intersections
register_items.consequence: Fire apparatus access turning radius unverified — road geometry not confirmed against IFC 503.2.4. The readable plan text shows road widths inferred at 24'–28' (not explicitly stated — width callouts are on D-6631-04, visual-only). IFC 503.2.4 requires minimum 20' inside / 40' outside turning radius for fire apparatus (Michigan local amendments commonly require 25'/48'). The water main sheets (D-6631-36, etc.) show fire hydrants spaced along all streets, confirming fire apparatus is intended to access all areas. Pull-through RV sites at 173' depth and 50.8' width create very wide roadway requirements at entry/exit points. The site plan (D-6631-04) could not be read to verify cul-de-sac geometry, T-turnaround provisions, or dead-end road lengths.
register_items.correction: If road widths are below 20' or turning radii are insufficient, the fire marshal will not issue a certificate of occupancy. Retrofit widening of paved roads in an occupied community costs $50,000–$200,000+ depending on extent and whether utilities must be relocated.
register_items.resolves: Before earthwork: EOR must provide a written certification (or annotated D-6631-04 print) confirming: (a) minimum 20' clear travel width on all roads; (b) IFC-compliant turning radius at every dead-end and cul-de-sac; (c) turnaround provisions on any dead-end road exceeding 150'. Coordinate with Manistee County or local fire authority for their specific radius requirement. If widths are deficient, road section must be widened before grading begins.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record + Fire Marshal pre-approval.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Fire apparatus access is a life-safety code item reviewed by the fire marshal as a condition of occupancy. Any width or radius deficiency discovered post-construction requires a code variance or physical correction before CO.
register_items.rom: Fire marshal pre-application meeting → EOR certification letter → fire marshal written approval before grading. Hold point: no road subgrade work until fire access confirmation received.

register_items.description: All sites — ADA accessible sites
register_items.consequence: No ADA-accessible sites identified anywhere in the plan set. The readable parcel dimension sheets (D-6631-07, 08, 09) show no ADA callout on any lot. The parcel type sheet (D-6631-06) is unreadable. Under the Fair Housing Act (FHA) and ADA, a residential rental community with 155 sites must provide accessible sites and accessible routes. For a rental MH/RV community, FHA requires accessible features on a minimum of the first-floor units; HUD and state guidance for MH communities typically requires 5% of sites to meet accessibility standards plus accessible routes to common facilities. No accessible route, accessible parking, or accessible site is visible in any readable sheet.
register_items.correction: Certificate of occupancy will be withheld pending ADA/FHA compliance review. Retrofitting accessible routes, pads, and reduced-slope site approaches after paving is complete costs $5,000–$15,000 per site plus accessible route paving work. Federal fair housing complaint exposure if none provided at opening.
register_items.resolves: Before site grading: EOR must identify on D-6631-04 and D-6631-06 the minimum 5% of sites designated accessible (≈8 sites), their locations, pad slopes (≤2% in any direction per ANSI A117.1), accessible route from each site to the bathhouse/office/amenities, and van-accessible parking at the office/clubhouse. ADA-compliant sites should be on the flattest terrain nearest to amenities. Submit to local building official and/or MSHDA for review if applicable.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — mandatory before grading plan is finalized.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: FHA/ADA accessibility is a federal compliance requirement. A site-plan revision identifying accessible sites and routes must be issued before building permit issuance (if applicable to site infrastructure) or before occupancy. Cannot be resolved by field decision.
register_items.rom: EOR plan revision → local building official or FHA consultant review → revised grading plan for accessible sites.

register_items.description: All streets — no stormwater detention visible
register_items.consequence: No stormwater detention or retention facility is shown or referenced anywhere in the 49-sheet plan set. All storm sewer profiles terminate at labeled POE (Point of Egress) locations — California Drive at STA 24+02 (POE) and Tennessee Avenue at STA 28+74 (POE). For a project disturbing what is likely 30–50+ acres adjacent to Manistee Lake, Michigan Part 31 (Water Resources Protection Act) and Manistee County stormwater ordinance will almost certainly require quantity control (detention) and quality control (water quality basin or equivalent) before discharge. Discharge from a 155-site impervious development directly off a bluff to a Great Lakes tributary without detention would trigger EGLE review and likely denial of the stormwater permit. No NPDES/SESC permit conditions or stormwater management report is referenced in any readable sheet.
register_items.correction: Stormwater permit will not be issued as designed. If constructed without detention, EGLE enforcement action (stop-work order, restoration order, civil penalty) is likely. Bluff-edge discharge of undetained stormwater accelerates bluff erosion — a documented catastrophic failure mode on Lake Michigan bluffs.
register_items.resolves: Before earthwork/grading: EOR must provide a stormwater management report demonstrating compliance with Michigan Part 31 and local ordinance for pre/post runoff rates and volumes. If detention is required (almost certain), a basin must be sized, located, and shown on revised plans. Outlet structure must include water quality treatment (extended detention or wet pond). Bluff discharge point must be stabilized with riprap or energy dissipation. Do not begin grading until EGLE/county stormwater permit is in hand.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record + EGLE + Manistee County.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Michigan Part 31 NPDES stormwater permit and Part 91 SESC permit are both required for this project scale. Missing detention is a permit-level deficiency that cannot be resolved by field decision. EGLE will not issue a permit for direct undetained discharge from a 30–50 acre impervious site.
register_items.rom: EGLE pre-application meeting → stormwater management report → basin design → permit application → permit issuance before grading. This is potentially the longest-lead permit item on the project.

register_items.description: Entire site — vertical structures
register_items.consequence: No clubhouse, bathhouse, office, maintenance building, dump station, or other amenity structure appears anywhere in the 49-sheet plan set. The plan index on D-6631-01 lists only civil infrastructure sheets. For a 155-site resort-quality MH/RV community, a bathhouse is not optional — Michigan DNR camping rules and most county health codes require toilet and shower facilities for seasonal RV sites. A dump station is required for any RV site without full hookup, and may be required even with full hookup under some county health codes. The absence of these structures from a bid-ready document set means either (a) they are in a separate package not coordinated with this civil set, or (b) they have been omitted from the project scope.
register_items.correction: If built as drawn with no bathhouse or dump station, occupancy permits for RV sites will be refused by Manistee County Health Department. If in a separate package, civil rough-ins (sewer stub, water stub, electrical conduit, grading) for those buildings must be installed during site grading — if the separate package is not coordinated with this civil set, stubs will be missing and roadway/grading will have to be cut open after paving.
register_items.resolves: Before bid: Owner must clarify whether vertical structures are in scope. If separate package exists, EOR must issue a utility rough-in coordination sheet showing: location of each amenity structure, sewer service stub size and invert, water service size, electrical conduit routing, and finished floor elevation. If no separate package exists, a bathhouse design must be completed and permitted before site occupancy.
register_items.permit: Owner decision + Engineer of Record coordination.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Bathhouse and dump station are health department and building permit items. Manistee County Health Department will not issue a campground license without approved sanitary facilities. Cannot be resolved by field decision.
register_items.rom: Owner clarification → separate architect/MEP engagement if needed → utility rough-in coordination added to civil set → building permit application.

register_items.description: All sanitary sewer mains — manhole spacing
register_items.consequence: Sanitary sewer manhole spacing exceeds Michigan standard on several reaches. Michigan Act 399 / EGLE sanitary sewer design standards require manholes at maximum 400-foot intervals on 8" sewers, plus at every change of pipe direction, grade, or size. Reading the visible reach lengths: California Drive shows 375 LF and 198.3 LF segments (Sheet D-6631-22), Oregon Avenue shows 223 LF and 150 LF (D-6631-25), Kentucky Avenue shows 270 LF + 270 LF = 540 LF between named manholes KA2 and KA3 (D-6631-26), and Tennessee Avenue shows 248 + 224 + 331 LF segments (D-6631-24). The 540 LF reach on Kentucky Avenue between KA2 (STA 4+29) and KA3 (not explicitly stationed) potentially exceeds the 400 LF maximum. Additionally, Oregon Avenue Station 13+32 (OA3) to 14+82 (OA4) = 150 LF (fine), but OA3 invert 648.34 with rim 663.25 = 14.91' deep manhole — unusually deep, requiring confined-space and safety provisions not called out in the readable details.
register_items.correction: Spacing violation: EGLE will not approve the sewer extension permit with >400 LF spacing. An additional manhole on Kentucky Avenue adds ~$5,000–$8,000 but avoids a permit rejection. Deep manhole: without confined-space callout in the specifications, the contractor may not price appropriate access equipment; a worker entry into an unvented 15' deep manhole is an OSHA confined-space fatality risk.
register_items.resolves: Kentucky Avenue: EOR must add an intermediate manhole at approximately STA 3+30 on Kentucky Avenue (midpoint of the 540 LF reach) to bring spacing to ≤270 LF each side. Oregon Avenue OA3: EOR must add a confined-space entry note and specify safety ladder, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 compliance, and ventilation requirements in the project specifications for any manhole >10' deep. Contractor must price confined-space equipment for all manholes deeper than 10'.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — RFI or field directive for manhole addition; specification addition for confined-space.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: The Act 399 permit application must show compliant manhole spacing. If the permit was issued with 540 LF spacing shown, EGLE may require a revision. EOR must confirm whether the permit was already issued with this spacing; if so, a minor revision letter to EGLE is needed.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR plan revision → EGLE revision letter if permit already issued → revised bid documents.

register_items.description: Oregon Ave OA3 (STA 13+32, RIM 663.25, INV 648.34); Washington Ave OA1 (STA 6+85, RIM 664.70, INV 649.85)
register_items.consequence: Extreme sanitary manhole depths — structural and OSHA risk not addressed. OA3: rim 663.25 − invert 648.34 = 14.91 ft deep. OA1: rim 664.70 − invert 649.85 = 14.85 ft deep. Several other manholes also appear to be 10–14 ft deep based on the rim/invert differential pattern (the sewer runs at 0.40% slope from high rims on these cross-streets down to the main trunk at lower elevation). Deep manholes (>12 ft) require precast risers, safety steps per OSHA, confined-space entry procedures, and potentially custom fabrication if standard 48" precast sections do not achieve the required depth with standard ring configurations.
register_items.correction: Without OSHA-compliant safety provisions specified: contractor may under-bid the work, or a worker may enter an unsafe manhole. A 15-ft deep, 48" diameter precast manhole in variable soil (bluff terrain — possible sandy or fill soils) also has a significantly higher risk of excavation cave-in than a standard 6-ft manhole. OSHA 29 CFR 1926.650 (excavation/trenching) requires shoring or sloping for any excavation >5 ft — at 15 ft depth in potentially loose bluff soils, this is a serious safety concern.
register_items.resolves: EOR must: (1) Add a note to D-6631-31 (Sanitary Details) specifying OSHA-compliant confined-space and excavation shoring requirements for all manholes >10 ft depth; (2) List all manholes >10 ft depth in a depth table with required shoring method; (3) Confirm precast manhole barrel sections are specified for full depth (standard 4-ft sections may not achieve 15 ft without custom order — verify with precast supplier). Contractor: provide a trench safety plan for all deep manholes as a specific bid line item, not bundled into general conditions.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record for specification addition; Contractor for site-specific trench safety plan.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans if EOR adds as a specification note — no agency resubmittal required if depth was already shown in the permit application. If depth was understated in the EGLE permit, notify EGLE.
register_items.rom: EOR specification note → contractor trench safety plan submission → hold point: county or MIOSHA trench safety inspection required before backfill at any manhole >10 ft depth.

register_items.description: California Drive STA 15+00 to 24+02 — storm and sanitary parallel routing
register_items.consequence: Storm sewer (12" HDPE @ 0.26%) and sanitary sewer (8" PVC @ 0.40%) run in parallel on California Drive for approximately 800–900 LF, with no horizontal or vertical separation dimensions called out in the readable profile text. Michigan Act 399 and EGLE standards require a minimum 10 feet of horizontal separation between water and sewer, and ASCE/AWWA standard requires 18 inches of vertical clearance at crossings. The profile sheets show both utilities in the same corridor but do not explicitly call out the separation distance. The storm invert at CD102 (STA 18+12) is 658.94 (12" storm, south inv) while the sanitary invert at CD3 (STA 18+01, nearby) is 656.74 (8" san, south inv) — a vertical gap of only ~2.2 ft, which is adequate at that station, but the horizontal separation over the 800 LF shared corridor is unconfirmed.
register_items.correction: If horizontal separation is less than 10 ft, EGLE Act 399 permit will cite the design. At a crossing or close approach with less than 18" vertical clearance, contamination risk from sewer exfiltration to storm is a regulatory and public health violation.
register_items.resolves: EOR must: (1) Add a horizontal separation callout on both the storm and sanitary profiles for California Drive confirming ≥10 ft separation throughout the shared corridor; (2) Verify at all crossing points that the vertical separation is ≥18" (storm below sewer preferred); (3) If any crossing has less than 18" vertical clearance, specify either an encasement pipe for the sewer or a crossed-under storm configuration with a minimum 18" clearance maintained.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — RFI.
register_items.documentation: EOR letter required: EGLE Act 399 permit application requires separation distances to be confirmed. If the permit was issued without this callout, EOR must submit a separation compliance letter. No agency resubmittal required if separations are confirmed to meet standards.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR separation confirmation letter → Add separation note to record drawings.

register_items.description: Water main — fire hydrant spacing
register_items.consequence: Fire hydrant spacing cannot be confirmed as compliant with IFC 507.5.1 from the readable plan text. Hydrants are shown at the following approximate stations: D-6631-36 STA 1+30; D-6631-39 STA 1+41; D-6631-40 STA 0+37; D-6631-42 STA 0+37 and STA 3+59; D-6631-43 STA 0+78, STA 3+00, STA 5+50 — minimum 8–10 confirmed hydrants across the development. IFC 507.5.1 requires hydrants within 400 feet of all portions of a building (or within 600 ft for one- and two-family detached). For an MH community, the Michigan State Housing Development Authority and local fire marshal typically apply the 400-ft standard. The overall utility plan (D-6631-11, unreadable) would show whether all sites are within 400 ft of a hydrant — this cannot be confirmed from the profile sheets alone. At least one large block (the northern pull-through RV area, Sites 248–256 range based on D-6631-09 dimension data) appears to be at the far end of Tennessee Avenue at STA 28+74 — a significant distance from the nearest confirmed hydrant callout.
register_items.correction: If any site is more than 400 ft from a hydrant, the fire marshal will not issue a CO for that portion of the development. Retrofitting a hydrant connection to an already-paved street requires opening the pavement and pressure-tapping the water main — $15,000–$40,000 per added hydrant including pavement restoration.
register_items.resolves: Before water main installation: EOR must provide a fire hydrant coverage map overlaid on D-6631-04 showing a 400 ft radius circle from every hydrant. Any site not within a 400 ft radius requires an additional hydrant. All hydrants must be on the 6" main and confirm minimum 1,500 GPM fire flow at 20 psi residual (verify with local water authority). Hydrant lead should be minimum 6" with a post indicator valve.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record + Fire Marshal pre-approval.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Fire flow and hydrant placement are life-safety items reviewed by the fire marshal. If hydrant locations must change, the revised layout must be submitted to the fire marshal before the water main is installed.
register_items.rom: Fire marshal hydrant coverage review → EOR revised hydrant map → fire marshal written approval → record drawing. Hold point: no water main installation until fire marshal approves hydrant layout.

register_items.description: Entire water distribution system — 6" main throughout
register_items.consequence: The entire new water distribution system uses 6" diameter main, including the primary collector/trunk feeding all streets. For a 155-site full-hookup development, the simultaneous demand calculation is critical. At 75 GPD per site (RV) to 200 GPD per site (MH) average daily demand, peak hourly demand at 3× average = 225–600 GPD/site × 155 sites / 24 hr × 3 = approximately 109–291 GPM peak flow through the trunk main. A 6" PVC C-900 water main at 5 ft/s velocity limit can carry approximately 445 GPM — adequate for demand. However, fire flow requires a residual pressure of ≥20 psi with 1,500 GPM flowing (IFC 507.3). At 1,500 GPM through a 6" main, head loss per 1,000 LF (Hazen-Williams C=150, 6" pipe) ≈ 120 ft — if the trunk main is >500 LF from the connection point, available fire flow at the far end of the system will be significantly less than 1,500 GPM at 20 psi. No hydraulic analysis is referenced or visible in the plan set.
register_items.correction: Without a hydraulic model confirming fire flow compliance at the most remote hydrant, the fire marshal and water authority cannot approve the system. If fire flow is inadequate at remote hydrants, the 6" trunk must be upsized to 8" or a looped system must be created. Looping or upsizing an already-installed water main is a major cost event.
register_items.resolves: Before water main installation: EOR must provide a hydraulic analysis (EPANET or equivalent) of the complete water distribution system showing: (a) peak domestic demand plus fire flow simultaneously at the most remote hydrant; (b) residual pressure ≥20 psi at all hydrant locations under fire flow condition; (c) system velocity ≤5 ft/s under all demand scenarios. If the model shows inadequate fire flow at remote locations, the trunk main (California Drive and Tennessee Avenue) must be upsized to 8". Submit hydraulic model to local water authority for review before installation.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — mandatory hydraulic analysis before bid.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: The local water authority and fire marshal must approve the hydraulic model. If main sizing changes, revised plans must be submitted. Cannot be resolved by field decision.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR hydraulic model → water authority and fire marshal review → revised bid documents if upsizing required.

register_items.description: All water main dead ends — multiple locations
register_items.consequence: Multiple water main dead ends are shown without flushing provisions (blow-offs). D-6631-32 shows "6"×6" TEE, 1-6" PLUG" at STA 0+00, indicating a capped tee. D-6631-33 shows "4+45 — 6"×6" TEE, 1-6" PLUG." D-6631-37 shows "0+00 — 6"×6" TEE, 1-6" PLUG." AWWA C651 and Michigan Act 399 require automatic or manual flush/blow-off valves at all dead ends to prevent bacteriological contamination from stagnant water. Plugged tees alone are not sufficient — they cannot be opened for flushing without breaking the connection.
register_items.correction: Stagnant water at dead ends will fail bacteriological testing (coliform positive results). System will not pass Michigan Act 399 disinfection requirements. Retroactive installation of blow-offs requires excavating the dead-end cap, installing a tee and blow-off assembly, and re-disinfecting the main — $3,000–$6,000 per dead end.
register_items.resolves: For every dead-end main shown with a plug: EOR must revise the detail to show a 2" blow-off assembly with a corporation stop, copper service, ball valve, and buried curb box accessible from grade — or for mains >6", a 2" NPT threaded tap on the plug itself with a hose-bib blow-off. AWWA standard blow-off detail must be added to D-6631-44 (Water Details). Contractor: install blow-offs before pressure testing and disinfection.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — specification and detail revision.
register_items.documentation: EOR letter required: Blow-off provisions are a standard EGLE Act 399 requirement. Adding them does not change the permit layout materially but should be documented in a revision letter to EGLE. No full resubmittal required.
register_items.rom: EOR detail revision → water main contractor instruction → hold point: all dead-end blow-offs installed and verified before pressure test and disinfection.

register_items.description: Electrical service — transformer sizing unconfirmed
register_items.consequence: No transformer schedule, kVA ratings, or transformer location plan is visible in any readable sheet. The project has an estimated load of 155 sites. Using connected load: if 80 MH sites at 200A/240V = 19,200W each (demand factor 0.4 per NEC 220.84) = 7,680W × 80 = 614 kW; if 75 RV sites at 50A/240V = 12,000W × 75 = 900 kW total RV; total estimated peak demand ≈ 1,200–1,500 kW (using utility diversity factors). Without a transformer schedule, it is impossible to verify that the transformers specified can carry this load, that secondary run lengths are within voltage-drop limits (NEC recommends ≤3% voltage drop on feeders, ≤5% total to outlet), or that the utility has been notified of the service size required.
register_items.correction: Undersized transformers will overload under peak demand (summer holiday weekend), causing transformer failure, potential fire, and extended outage affecting all sites on the affected transformer. Oversized transformers waste capital. Without a transformer schedule, the utility will not set equipment.
register_items.resolves: EOR must issue a complete transformer schedule showing: kVA per transformer, location, primary voltage, secondary voltage (120/240V 1Ø or 277/480V 3Ø if applicable), and the sites served by each transformer. EOR must also provide a voltage drop calculation confirming all secondary runs are within 3% from transformer to pedestal. Submit to utility (Consumers Energy or local co-op) for service design approval.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — mandatory before electrical bid.
register_items.documentation: EOR letter required: Transformer sizing must be approved by the serving utility before equipment is ordered. No agency resubmittal, but utility service design approval is a prerequisite for energization.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR transformer schedule → voltage drop calcs → utility service design approval → hold point: no transformer pad poured until utility confirms transformer size and location.

register_items.description: Parcel dimensions — road right-of-way width not labeled
register_items.consequence: No road right-of-way or pavement width dimension is called out on any readable dimension sheet. The dimension sheets (D-6631-07/08/09) show individual lot widths and depths extensively but the road corridor between lots is not dimensioned. Without explicit road width callouts, the paving contractor cannot confirm the pavement section width, the curb contractor cannot set forms, and the utility contractor cannot confirm clearance between the utility trench and the back of curb.
register_items.correction: The paving contractor will be forced to scale dimensions from D-6631-04 (an overall plan at small scale), creating a high probability of installation errors. If the road is paved at the wrong width, it cannot be corrected without removing and replacing curb and pavement.
register_items.resolves: EOR must add road width callouts to the dimension sheets or confirm they appear on D-6631-04 with sufficient clarity to field-lay the roads. The road cross-section sheet (if it exists — not found in the plan index) must show the full section including: lane width, curb type, gutter width, pavement thickness, base course thickness, and subgrade treatment. If no cross-section sheet exists, EOR must add one.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — plan revision or annotation.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans: Road width revision is a clarification of design intent, not a change to a permitted element. No agency resubmittal required unless a width change affects fire access (see E-03).
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR annotation → contractor instruction.

register_items.description: Entire site — geotechnical basis of design absent
register_items.consequence: No geotechnical report, soil boring log, or subgrade design recommendation is referenced in any readable plan sheet. The site is on a bluff above Manistee Lake — a geologically active environment with documented Lake Michigan bluff erosion, potential for sand or glacial outwash soils, and slope-stability concerns. Without a geotech report, the following design elements are unverifiable: (a) pavement section (no CBR/R-value basis); (b) MH pad foundation type (piers, runners, or mat — no bearing capacity basis); (c) utility trench bedding specifications (no native soil classification); (d) slope stability of any graded cut slopes near the bluff edge; (e) retaining wall requirements at grade transitions.
register_items.correction: If soil conditions are worse than assumed (loose sand, high water table, organic layers), pavement will fail within 2–3 years, MH pads will settle causing structural damage to homes, and utility trenches will have excessive infiltration. Bluff-edge grading without a slope-stability analysis creates risk of a catastrophic slope failure taking utilities or roads with it.
register_items.resolves: Before earthwork: Owner must commission a geotechnical investigation (minimum 5–8 borings to 20 ft depth across the development footprint, plus 2–3 borings near the bluff edge for slope stability analysis). Geotechnical engineer must provide: allowable bearing capacity, recommended pavement section, trench bedding classification, and slope stability FS ≥ 1.5 for all cut slopes within 200 ft of the bluff edge. All design elements must be reconciled with the geotech report before earthwork begins.
register_items.permit: Owner to commission geotechnical engineer; EOR to incorporate recommendations.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable for bluff-edge work: Michigan's Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act (Part 323, Shorelands Protection) and potentially Manistee County may require a slope stability analysis as a condition of any grading permit near the Lake Michigan shoreline. EGLE Coastal Zone Management may also have jurisdiction.
register_items.rom: Geotech firm engagement → field borings → report → EOR plan revision incorporating recommendations → hold point: no earthwork until geotech recommendations are incorporated into plans and contractor briefed.

register_items.description: All sites — pad drainage direction
register_items.consequence: Pad drainage direction and cross-slope cannot be verified from the readable plan text. For MH sites, the HUD Manufactured Home Installation Standard (24 CFR Part 3285) requires site surface drainage to direct water away from the home at a minimum 0.5% slope, and ANSI A225.1 requires surface drainage away from the perimeter of the home on all sides. For RV pull-through sites, the pad should drain at a minimum 1% slope perpendicular to the long axis toward the roadway or a defined swale — not toward adjacent sites or structures. Without the grading plan (not found), site pad slopes cannot be verified.
register_items.correction: Pads draining toward homes cause foundation moisture problems, wood rot, and mold — warranty and habitability issues. Pads draining toward adjacent sites create inter-site drainage conflicts. On the bluff, any uncontrolled runoff direction risks concentration at the bluff edge.
register_items.resolves: Before grading: EOR must provide finished-grade spot elevations at each site corner (or a grading plan showing pad slopes explicitly). Minimum site pad slope: 0.5% away from home on all four sides. No pad surface should drain toward an adjacent lot or toward a structure. Contractor: verify each pad is graded to drain correctly before concrete is poured.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — grading plan must be provided if not already in the set.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans if grading plan is provided and pads drain correctly — field correction is within EOR's design.
register_items.rom: RFI requesting grading plan → EOR response → contractor grading instruction.

register_items.description: California Drive STA 23+48 to 23+73 — vertical curve at low point
register_items.consequence: The California Drive profile (D-6631-13) shows a 50 ft vertical curve centered on PVI STA 23+48.28, with a low point at STA 23+68.74, El. 659.22, transitioning from +0.50% to a grade not fully legible. The inlet structure CD104 (SAN MH STR NO CD104, STA 23+62.5, RIM 659.36) has a rim only 0.14 ft above the road low point elevation (659.22). If the inlet is a stormwater structure at this station, a 0.14 ft rim-to-road-surface margin is within normal design tolerance — but if the road is designed with a finish grade at or above 659.22 and the inlet rim is at 659.36, there is a 0.14 ft sump before the inlet activates, which is acceptable. However, the gutter line elevation cannot be confirmed without the cross-section. Verification required: Confirm that the inlet rim at CD104 is at or below the gutter flowline elevation at STA 23+62, and that the road does not pond before reaching the inlet.
register_items.correction: If the inlet rim is 0.14 ft above the gutter flowline, stormwater will pond 0.14 ft deep in the travel lane before draining — unacceptable for a paved road and a potential icing hazard in Michigan winters.
register_items.resolves: Surveyor or EOR to confirm finished gutter elevation at STA 23+62. If gutter elevation is above inlet rim 659.36, lower the inlet frame and grate to match gutter flowline. If gutter elevation is below 659.22 road centerline low point, confirm the cross-slope directs flow to the inlet before the low point is reached.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — field measurement and confirmation.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans if inlet rim matches gutter flowline within ±0.02 ft.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR field confirmation → record drawing elevation note.

register_items.description: Oregon Avenue — 24" HDPE storm main (215 LF @ 0.30%)
register_items.consequence: The largest storm pipe in the readable plan set is a 24" HDPE on Oregon Avenue (D-6631-15, 215 LF @ 0.30%). This pipe transitions to 18" HDPE downstream (58 LF @ 0.30% and 207 LF @ 0.30%). A pipe size decrease from 24" to 18" downstream is a hydraulic red flag — standard practice requires storm sewer to increase in size (or remain the same) in the downstream direction as tributary area increases. A 24"-to-18" step-down will cause backwater and surcharge in the 24" section during design storm events, potentially causing road flooding at the Oregon Avenue/California Drive intersection.
register_items.correction: 24" pipe backing up behind an 18" restriction will surcharge and flood the road surface and adjacent sites during a 10-year or 25-year storm event. This is a design error that must be corrected before storm sewer installation.
register_items.resolves: EOR must review the Oregon Avenue storm sewer hydraulic design and confirm whether the 18" downstream of the 24" is hydraulically correct (possible if the 18" outlet is a very short section to a large outfall structure that controls the grade). If not hydraulically justified, the downstream pipe must be upsized to 24" or the upstream section downsized to match. Provide a drainage area map and pipe sizing calculation for Oregon Avenue.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — hydraulic review required.
register_items.documentation: EOR letter required: A pipe size reduction in the downstream direction is a design deviation from standard practice. EOR must certify hydraulic justification or revise. No agency resubmittal required if the design criteria (10/25-year event) is still met.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR hydraulic calculation review → pipe size revision if required → revised bid documents.

register_items.description: Entry road(s) — MH transport delivery route geometry
register_items.consequence: Manufactured homes (double-wide, up to 28' wide × 80' long) require a delivery route with minimum 15' vertical clearance, minimum 14' travel lane width (preferably 16'), and turning radii of minimum 75 ft outside radius. The entry road geometry and internal routing for MH delivery cannot be verified from the readable text. The dimension sheets show lots with 55'–80' frontages, suggesting the road corridor is wide enough — but tight curves at street intersections or a constricted site entrance could prevent MH delivery without tree/utility clearing not shown on the plans.
register_items.correction: If the delivery route geometry is inadequate, the transporter will refuse delivery. The developer will need to remove trees, relocate utilities, or widen roads to allow delivery — a potentially expensive surprise if discovered on the first delivery day.
register_items.resolves: Before site plan finalization: EOR and the MH transporter (or the developer's designated transport contractor) must perform a route analysis from the closest state highway to the last MH site, identifying any constraint (low wire, tight turn, narrow bridge, overhead structure). The internal road layout must be verified for 75 ft outside turning radius at every MH site approach. Any oversize structure permits required from MDOT must be identified early.
register_items.permit: Owner + MH transporter + EOR.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans — delivery route analysis is an operational coordination item, not a permit item, unless a road widening requires a right-of-way permit.
register_items.rom: Route analysis document → contractor/transporter notification → hold point: confirm delivery route is clear before first MH delivery is scheduled.

register_items.description: Service lateral locations and invert elevations not shown. The plan set shows main-line sewer (8" PVC) and manholes but does not show individual site service laterals in the readable text. For 155 sites, each site requires a 4" or 6" sanitary service lateral from the main to the site's sewer connection point (a stub-up at the MH pad, or a cleanout near the pedestal for RV). Without lateral locations and stub-up elevations, the utility contractor does not know where to install each lateral, and the grading contractor does not know where to protect the stub. Laterals installed at the wrong elevation will either not drain by gravity or will be too shallow for frost protection (Michigan frost depth ≥ 42").
register_items.consequence: Laterals installed in wrong location or at wrong elevation will require excavation and replacement after grading is complete — typically a $500–$2,000 per site repair. If laterals are too shallow, they will freeze in winter — service interruption and potential health code violation for a year-round community.
register_items.correction: EOR must add a utility rough-in plan sheet (or annotate D-6631-11) showing each site's lateral stub location, invert elevation, minimum cover (42" frost), and cap detail. Contractor: do not backfill any lateral until EOR has confirmed the stub elevation matches the site pad finished grade.
register_items.resolves: Engineer of Record — additional plan sheet required.
register_items.permit: Within approved plans — laterals are part of the permitted sewer system but their individual design is typically delegated to the contractor per EOR standard detail. A standard detail for lateral stub with frost depth and slope must be on D-6631-31.
register_items.documentation: RFI → EOR lateral detail confirmation → utility contractor instruction.
register_items.rom: Adding lateral detail sheet: $3,000–$8,000 EOR time. No construction cost impact if coordinated before installation.

register_items.location: D-6631-44 (partially readable), all water main sheets
register_items.description: Pipe material specification inconsistency — HDPE vs. PVC vs. DI not fully reconciled. The water main profile sheets show the water main material as implied PVC or DI (fittings referenced are standard PVC C-900 or DI mechanical joint types). The water detail sheet (D-6631-44) partially shows an "HDPE Connection Detail" alongside PVC/DI details. The storm sewer is clearly HDPE. The sanitary sewer is clearly PVC. The water main material is not explicitly stated in any readable callout — only fitting types are listed. If HDPE is intended for water main (an increasingly common practice), the fittings, thrust restraint, and disinfection procedures differ significantly from PVC C-900.
register_items.consequence: If the contractor installs the wrong pipe material, the system may not pass pressure testing, the utility may reject the material, or the fitting types will be incompatible. HDPE water main requires electrofusion or flanged connections — not the mechanical joint glands described in D-6631-44. Installing the wrong material will require removal and replacement of the entire water main.
register_items.correction: EOR must add a water main material callout to every water main profile sheet (e.g., "6" PVC C-900, DR-18" or "6" DI CL 52"). If HDPE is intended, the fitting schedule and connection details must be revised to match HDPE-compatible fittings. The bidding contractor must confirm pipe material with the EOR before ordering material.
register_items.resolves: Engineer of Record — specification clarification.
register_items.permit: Within approved plans if a clarification note is added. If material type changes from what was shown in the EGLE Act 399 permit, a permit amendment letter may be required.
register_items.documentation: RFI → EOR material specification note → contractor confirmation before pipe order. Hold point: no pipe installation until material is confirmed and EOR-approved submittals are received.
register_items.rom: No cost impact if material is correct from the start. Wrong material installed and removed: $40–$80/LF × 7,000 LF = $280,000–$560,000 worst case.

register_items.description: SESC Plan — erosion control at bluff-edge outfalls
register_items.consequence: The SESC Plan (D-6631-03) is not readable, but two storm sewer outfalls (POE) are identified at California Drive STA 24+02 and Tennessee Avenue STA 28+74. Both outfalls appear to be at or near the bluff edge above Manistee Lake. Michigan Part 91 (SESC) and Part 31 (Water Resources) require outfall stabilization (riprap apron, energy dissipator, or plunge pool) at every stormwater discharge point. For a bluff-edge outfall, additional requirements likely apply under EGLE Coastal Zone Management and potentially USACE Section 404 (if discharge reaches navigable waters of the US). The outfall protection details could not be read from D-6631-03.
register_items.correction: Unprotected bluff-edge outfall during and after construction will accelerate bluff erosion, potentially undermining the adjacent road and utility corridor, depositing sediment in Manistee Lake (a state designated resource), and triggering EGLE enforcement. Lake Michigan bluff erosion is an active and documented regulatory concern in Manistee County.
register_items.resolves: Before construction: EOR must confirm outfall protection details are shown on D-6631-03. If not present, add: (a) riprap apron sized for the design storm velocity (typically 5–10 ft apron length, Class II or III riprap); (b) energy dissipator for pipes discharging at >5 ft/s; (c) silt curtain in Manistee Lake during construction if any grading extends to the bluff edge; (d) geotextile at bluff face where discharge is directed. Coordinate with EGLE Coastal Zone office and USACE before construction at the bluff face.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record + EGLE + USACE coordination.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable: Any work at the bluff face or discharge to Manistee Lake may require a Part 325 (Inland Lakes and Streams) permit from EGLE and/or USACE Section 404 permit. These are separate from the Part 91 SESC permit.
register_items.rom: Pre-application meeting with EGLE Coastal Zone → EGLE Part 325 permit application if required → USACE Section 404 pre-application if required → outfall protection detail on record drawings.

register_items.description: Water main — Michigan water/sewer crossing separation at all sewer crossings
register_items.consequence: At multiple locations, the water main and sanitary sewer are in close proximity or crossing. For example, D-6631-39 shows the water main (FL 660.1–660.5) in the same corridor as "PROP 18" STM SWR INV 657.53" and "PROP 8" SAN SWR INV 658.34" within the same reach. The water main at D-6631-39 is at approximately FL 660.1–660.5 with the sanitary sewer invert at 658.34 — a vertical gap of approximately 1.6–2.1 ft between the sewer crown and water main invert. AWWA M51 and Michigan Act 399 require ≥18" vertical clearance at crossings with the water main above the sewer. The clearance here appears to be approximately 18"–24" (sewer OD of 8" pipe = crown at ~659.1, water main at 660.1 = ~12" clearance) — potentially less than the required 18".
register_items.correction: Less than 18" separation at a water-over-sewer crossing is an Act 399 violation and a public health risk (sewer exfiltration can contaminate the water main at the crossing). EGLE will not approve a system with less than 18" clearance unless a 20 LF DI sewer encasement is provided.
register_items.resolves: EOR must check all water/sewer crossings and confirm ≥18" vertical clearance (water above sewer) or provide a 20 LF DI or HDPE pipe encasement of the sewer at the crossing per Act 399. Add a crossing detail to D-6631-44 (Water Details) or D-6631-31 (Sanitary Details) showing the encasement method and clearance requirement.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — crossing detail required.
register_items.documentation: EOR letter required: If any crossing is less than 18", the EGLE permit must include the encasement detail. A crossing-clearance table in the permit application is standard practice.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR crossing clearance confirmation → encasement detail added → EGLE permit compliance confirmation.

register_items.description: Electrical — RV pedestal amperage by site type not specified
register_items.consequence: No RV pedestal specification (50A/30A/20A combination or all-50A) is visible in any readable sheet. Modern full-hookup RV super sites typically require 50A/240V service at minimum; many operators also provide 30A and 20A outlets on the same pedestal. The electrical detail on D-6631-49 shows a 100A single-phase service that appears to be an MH panel — no RV pedestal detail is visible. Without a pedestal specification, the electrical contractor will provide whatever they typically install, which may not match the operator's service offering or the guest's expectations for a "super site."
register_items.correction: If only 30A service is installed on a super site, guests with 50A coaches (the large majority of luxury RV market) will be unable to run both HVAC units simultaneously. This is a guest experience failure and a revenue risk — super site premium pricing requires 50A service. Retrofitting pedestals after installation: $500–$1,500 per site.
register_items.resolves: EOR must add an RV pedestal schedule to the electrical plan or D-6631-49 specifying: amperage (50A/30A/20A or all-50A), voltage (120/240V), NEMA outlet configuration (14-50R for 50A, L14-30 or TT-30 for 30A), weatherproof enclosure rating (minimum NEMA 3R), and whether metering is individual or master. Owner should confirm service level with the resort operator before finalizing.
register_items.permit: Owner decision → Engineer of Record specification.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans — pedestal type selection is a specification item, not a permitted design element. No agency resubmittal.

register_items.description: Entire site — site numbering sequence gaps
register_items.consequence: The site numbering visible across all readable sheets contains gaps in the proposed sequence. Numbers visible: 1, 9, 16–38, 39–55, 78–103, 169–256 (with internal gaps). Numbers 2–8, 10–15, 56–77, 104–168 are not visible in any readable sheet as proposed sites — they either exist only on the visual-only D-6631-04, belong to existing sites with different prefixes, or represent a numbering scheme with intentional gaps. If the gaps represent real lots that exist on D-6631-04 but were not extracted, the total site count could be higher than 155. If the gaps are intentional (e.g., reserved for future phases or existing sites renumbered), the count is 155 as described.
register_items.correction: A higher actual site count than 155 could affect the stormwater permit (impervious area), the Act 399 sanitary permit (design flow), and the EGLE campground license (number of licensed sites). A lower count would not affect permits but would create confusion during construction inspection.
register_items.resolves: Before mobilization: EOR must provide a numbered site list (lot schedule) confirming the total count of new proposed sites and the site-numbering key. The lot schedule should appear on D-6631-06 (Parcel Types). If D-6631-06 does not contain a lot schedule, EOR must issue one as an addendum.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — lot schedule confirmation.
register_items.documentation: Agency notification unavoidable if count differs from 155: If any permit was issued based on 155 sites and the actual count differs, all quantity-based permits (sewer, stormwater, EGLE campground) must be amended.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR lot schedule → comparison against all permit applications.

register_items.description: General notes — undefined abbreviations
register_items.consequence: The line type legend on D-6631-02 was partially extracted but appears to cut off mid-list. Several standard abbreviations are defined (BC, BM, CB, CL, CJ, CMP, CSP, DI, etc.) but the full list is not readable. If abbreviations used on the construction drawings are not in the legend (e.g., "POE" appears in sheet titles without definition in the readable notes text, "SESC" is used without formal definition on the drawings, "VIF" on D-6631-49 is not in the readable legend), field crews may misinterpret.
register_items.correction: Minor interpretation risk. VIF ("Verify in Field") on the electrical detail — if left unresolved, the electrical contractor may make incorrect field decisions about utility connection points.
register_items.resolves: EOR to confirm the full abbreviation list on D-6631-02 is complete and that "POE," "VIF," "SESC," "MDOT," and all other abbreviations used throughout the set are defined. Issue a complete general notes sheet as a bid addendum if the printed D-6631-02 is incomplete.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — documentation.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans.
register_items.rom: Addendum to bid documents.

register_items.description: California Drive STA 18+12 and 18+13 — storm and sanitary structure at same station
register_items.consequence: STR NO CD102 (storm, 48" DIA, STA 18+12.4, RIM 665.45, INV 658.94) and SAN MH #CD3 (sanitary, STA 18+01.7, RIM 665.31, INV 656.74) are located within 11.7 ft of each other at the same general station. The storm structure is 48" diameter and the sanitary MH is also presumably 48" — two large concrete structures within ~12 ft of each other in the same trench corridor. Michigan Act 399 requires 10 ft horizontal separation between water and sewer, but does not specify storm-to-sanitary separation. However, placing two 48" structures within 12 ft of each other creates a shoring challenge and potential interference during excavation. The RIM elevation difference (665.45 vs. 665.31 = 0.14 ft) is within normal tolerance.
register_items.correction: Excavation conflict and shoring complexity — not a design failure but a constructability risk. If the contractor excavates for both structures simultaneously without adequate shoring in loose bluff soils, trench collapse is possible.
register_items.resolves: Before excavation: GC must develop a trench safety plan that addresses the two-structure cluster at STA 18+00–18+13. Shoring for both structures simultaneously may require a wider trench box or soldier-pile system. Sequencing: install storm structure first (deeper excavation), then sanitary MH, or vice versa with appropriate temporary shoring left in place.
register_items.permit: GC field plan — contractor responsible for trench safety method.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans.
register_items.rom: Contractor trench safety plan submission → hold point: MIOSHA trench inspection at STA 18+00 before backfill if >5 ft depth.

register_items.description: California Drive STA 24+00 to 24+02 — POE labeling
register_items.consequence: The storm sewer sheet (D-6631-13) ends at "STA 24+02 (POE)" and the sanitary sheet (D-6631-23) also ends at STA 24+00 with "SAN MH #CD5." The POE for storm is labeled but the actual discharge structure, end section, riprap, or energy dissipator is not called out in the readable text — the sheet simply ends. Similarly, the sanitary connection point at STA 24+00 is labeled but the tie-in to the existing system is not detailed. These are the most critical construction endpoints on California Drive and they have the least detail.
register_items.correction: Field crew will not know what end treatment to install at the storm outfall or how to make the sanitary connection. This is not a safety or functional error if standard details cover it — but if the standard detail is on D-6631-21 (Storm Details, visual-only) or D-6631-31 (Sanitary Details, visual-only) and those sheets are not clear to field crews, the connection will be made incorrectly.
register_items.resolves: Before construction at STA 24+00: Confirm D-6631-21 contains an end-section and riprap apron detail that covers the California Drive outfall. Confirm D-6631-31 contains a connection-to-existing sanitary detail. If not, EOR must issue details for these two connection points specifically.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — detail confirmation.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans if standard details cover these conditions.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR detail confirmation → field crew briefing at pre-construction meeting.

register_items.description: Minnesota Avenue — 7 LF of 12" HDPE storm sewer @ 0.50%
register_items.consequence: Minnesota Avenue shows only 7 LF of 12" HDPE storm sewer (D-6631-17). This is an extremely short storm pipe reach — either a stub to a future extension, a very short connection between two structures, or a possible data extraction error (7 LF may be part of a larger number cut off in the text). A 7 LF pipe segment has no practical standalone function and will likely be missed in a quantity take-off.
register_items.correction: If 7 LF is correct, it is a stub that needs a cap or connection. If it is a transcription error from the drawing, the actual quantity may be significantly different, affecting the storm sewer bid item.
register_items.resolves: EOR must confirm the Minnesota Avenue storm sewer length is correct as stated. If 7 LF is correct, show both end conditions (structure connection and capped stub). If incorrect, provide the correct length.
register_items.permit: Engineer of Record — quantity verification.
register_items.documentation: Within approved plans.
register_items.rom: RFI → EOR confirmation → bid quantity clarification.
